notes: Company background: mid-market SaaS (product analytics) with 450 employees, heavy search & discovery use in product UI
Primary goal: replace brittle keyword search with dense vector similarity across product docs and user events
POC approach: start on Hosted API to iterate quickly, then move to Dedicated for production predictability and data isolation

Throughput targets (customer-provided): target 50 QPS for semantic search (nearline), bulk embed throughput of 2k vectors/min for ongoing backfill, nightly batch of ~1.8M texts (2M vectors) to run over several hours
Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 120ms for a 64-vector similarity query under expected production load

Vector DB integration: currently prototype with Postgres+pgvector; evaluating managed vector DBs (Pinecone) vs self-hosted (Milvus/Weaviate). Wants Redwood guidance on connector patterns and bulk write performance
Cost sensitivity: mid-market buyer, wants clear per-embedding/unit economics; very focused on cost of nightly batch jobs and storage/replica costs
Security: must be SOC2-compliant vendor, SSO/SAML mandatory, data residency = US-only for PII-containing segments, audit logs required
Quote from CTO (L. Ramos): 'We need predictable tail latency. If the vector pipeline stalls during a backfill, product will break. We need a plan that scales.'

SE notes: suggested two-step POC: 1) validate embedding quality + vector DB indexing on Hosted API; 2) run production throughput test and measure end-to-end latency with a realistic shard size. Recommend prefix caching and batch embed pipeline with asynchronous retries
Demo feedback: liked streaming + structured output examples. Concerned about Dedicated minimums and how autoscaling works during burst (QA + release peaks)
Procurement: finance needs a clear TCO comparison Hosted vs Dedicated for 12 months (include burst pricing). Draft pricing shared (drive link)

Success criteria for POC: embedding recall >= baseline, 95th pctl latency < 120ms at 50 QPS, nightly batch completes within SLA window (4 hours), and integration with pgvector or Pinecone with no data-loss
